items.title: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes near Tonga; no tsunami threat

featured_image.name: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake rattles Neiafu, Tonga

items.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Tonga in the South Pacific on Tuesday, according to the United States Geological Survey, but the deep tremor prompted no tsunami warning and there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.

items.title: AWS Bahrain region disrupted by drones for second time this month

featured_image.name: Drone strikes damage Amazon data centres in UAE and Bahrain ...

items.description:
Amazon said on Monday that its Amazon Web Services cloud computing region in Bahrain has "been disrupted" due to drone activity, marking the second time the facility has been hit since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran earlier this month.[1][2]

The disruption was first reported by Reuters, with an Amazon spokesperson confirming that the outage stemmed from drone activity in the area. Amazon said it is helping to migrate customers to alternate AWS regions while it works to recover, though the company did not disclose the extent of the damage or provide a timeline for restoration.[2][1]

"As this situation evolves and, as we have advised before, we request those with workloads in the affected regions continue to migrate to other locations," Amazon said in a statement Monday night.[2]

items.title: ISS images of Russian missile strike on Kyiv verified by analysts

featured_image.name: ISS captures images of Russian missile strike on Kyiv from space

items.description:
Images taken from the International Space Station appear to show Russian ballistic missiles streaking toward Kyiv and being intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses, offering a rare space-based view of the war that has gripped analysts and the public alike.

The photographs, captured by an ISS-mounted camera on December 27, 2025, show two luminous trails moving from the northeast toward the Ukrainian capital before vanishing amid bursts of explosions in and around the city. The footage was compiled into a timelapse by Italian space enthusiast Riccardo Rossi of the AstronautiCAST YouTube channel and first published on February 23, 2026, quickly spreading through Ukrainian open-source intelligence channels on the eve of the war's fourth anniversary.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil prices swing as Iran denies Trump's claim of war talks

featured_image.name: Trump to postpone strikes on Iranian power plants for five days

items.description: Oil prices swung wildly on Monday as President Donald Trump claimed the United States held "productive conversations" with Iran aimed at ending the four-week-old war, only for Tehran to flatly deny any negotiations took place. The conflicting signals sent crude benchmarks tumbling from recent highs before partially recovering, while Wall Street rallied on hopes for a diplomatic resolution.

items.title: Australia, EU poised to finalize free trade deal after nearly a decade of talks

featured_image.name: EU and Australia strike free trade deal after years of talks

items.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Australia on Monday for a three-day visit aimed at concluding a free trade agreement that has been under negotiation since 2018. Von der Leyen is set to meet Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Tuesday, with both sides signaling they are close to finalizing a deal that would also include a new security and defense partnership.[1][2]

items.title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf ID'd as Trump negotiation partner

featured_image.name: thumbs_b_c_82d6fe7a4bd6e069b97c337d7a26ff5e.jpg?v=103723

items.description:
Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has been identified by U.S. and Israeli sources as the Iranian official at the center of talks with American envoys, even as Tehran flatly denies any negotiations are taking place and Ghalibaf himself dismissed the reports as "fake news."

President Donald Trump announced Monday that he was ordering a five-day pause on planned strikes against Iran's power plants and energy infrastructure, saying the U.S. had held "very good and productive conversations" with Iranian counterparts over the preceding two days. Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner had been in discussions with "a top person" in Iran but refused to identify the individual, saying he did not want that person to be killed.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Colombian military plane crashes after takeoff, killing at least one

featured_image.name: Colombia military plane crash: 110 soldiers on board

items.description:
A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane carrying 125 people crashed moments after takeoff Monday morning in the country's remote southern Amazon region, killing at least one person, injuring 77 others, and leaving more than 40 still unaccounted for as rescue operations continued into the evening.

The aircraft went down about two kilometers from the airport in Puerto Leguízamo, a municipality in the Amazonian province of Putumayo near the borders of Peru and Ecuador, according to Defense Minister Pedro Sánchez, who disclosed the crash on X and called it a "tragic accident." The Lockheed Martin-built plane was transporting 114 soldiers and 11 crew members to another city in Putumayo province when it encountered an unspecified problem and plunged to the ground.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Claude can now point, click and navigate your Mac like a human user

featured_image.name: Anthropic Says New AI Model Is Better at Using Computers ...

items.description: Anthropic is rolling out new capabilities that allow its Claude AI to directly control Mac computers, pointing, clicking, and navigating applications the way a human user would. The update, arriving March 23 for Claude Pro and Max subscribers as a research preview, brings computer-use features to both Claude Cowork and Claude Code on macOS.[1]

items.title: Israel used Iran's own street cameras to track and kill Khamenei

featured_image.name: Inside the US-Israel plan to kill Iran’s Khamenei

items.description:
Israel exploited Tehran's vast network of street cameras — hacked years earlier — to track Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and confirm his location before the February 28 airstrike that killed him, according to an Associated Press investigation published Monday based on interviews with intelligence officials familiar with the operation.[1][2]

The revelation underscores how surveillance infrastructure built by authoritarian governments to monitor dissent can be turned into a weapon against them.

items.title: Chevron CEO says oil market underpricing Hormuz closure

featured_image.name: Chevron CEO says Iran war impact isn't fully priced into oil market

items.description:
Chevron CEO Mike Wirth said Monday that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has inflicted greater damage on global oil and gas markets than the Russia-Ukraine war, warning that rebuilding supply chains and inventories will take considerable time even after the critical waterway reopens.

"We've got a lot of oil and gas now that is not flowing into the market," Wirth said at the CERAWeek by S&P Global conference in Houston. "Physical supply chains don't respond immediately, so even if the strait opens at some point, it will take time to rebuild inventories of the right grades of crude and the right types of fuel."[1]

items.title: Bahrain seeks UN approval of force to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: At least 30 warships needed to open Strait of Hormuz amid Iran blockade,  sources say | The Standard

items.description:
The UN Security Council on Monday began consultations on a draft resolution that would authorize the use of military force to secure the Strait of Hormuz, as a growing coalition of nations declared their willingness to help reopen the vital waterway that Iran has effectively shut down since late February.

The draft, circulated by Bahrain, invokes Chapter VII of the UN Charter — which grants the council authority to sanction actions ranging from targeted sanctions to the use of force — and would permit member states to employ "all necessary means" in and around the strait, according to a text seen by Reuters. The mandate would extend to the territorial waters of bordering states, with the aim of ensuring transit passage and deterring attempts to disrupt international navigation.[1]

items.title: Pakistan emerges as lead mediator between US and Iran

featured_image.name: Pakistan's Premier Sharif in Saudi Arabia after phone call with Iranian  president amid Mideast tensions

items.description:
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday, expressing solidarity with the Iranian people amid the ongoing war in the Gulf region and calling for urgent collective efforts to de-escalate tensions through dialogue and diplomacy.[1][2]

The call came as Pakistan positioned itself as a lead mediator between the United States and Iran, with the Financial Times reporting that Pakistani army chief Asim Munir spoke directly with President Donald Trump on Sunday about the conflict. Senior Pakistani officials have been back-channeling communications between Tehran and Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to the Financial Times, with Pakistan pitching Islamabad as a possible venue for talks as early as this week.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Estee Lauder confirms merger talks with Spain's Puig

featured_image.name: Estee Lauder in discussions with Puig for a combination (EL ...

items.description:
Estée Lauder confirmed Monday that it is in discussions over a potential business combination with Puig, the Barcelona-based beauty group behind Charlotte Tilbury, Carolina Herrera, and Jean Paul Gaultier. The deal, first reported by the Financial Times, could be announced as soon as Monday and would create a combined entity valued at more than $40 billion, according to reports from Bloomberg and Investing.com.[1][2][3]

In a statement, Estée Lauder said the two companies would "potentially merge their businesses," but cautioned that "no final decision has been made, and no agreement has been reached". Puig separately confirmed that negotiations are underway. Shares of Estée Lauder fell as much as 9.1% on the news, while Puig's stock rose roughly 3%.[4][5][6][7][8][9]

items.title: Antarctic microbes survive from -20°C to 75°C by feeding on air

featured_image.name: Microbes in Antarctica survive the freezing and dark winter by living ...

items.description: Microorganisms buried in Antarctic soil can sustain themselves by feeding on trace gases in the atmosphere across a temperature range spanning 95 degrees Celsius, from minus 20°C to 75°C, according to new research from Australia's Monash University published in The ISME Journal.[1][2]

items.title: China urges US, Israel to halt Middle East fighting, warns of 'vicious cycle'

featured_image.name: China urges caution in Israel-Iran tensions, calls for ceasefire | Reuters

items.description:
China on Monday urged all parties in the Middle East conflict, particularly the United States and Israel, to cease military operations, warning that continued fighting risks a "vicious cycle" that could plunge the region into chaos and drag down the global economy, according to Reuters.[1]

The warning came as President Donald Trump extended a 48-hour deadline he had imposed on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, postponing threatened strikes on Iranian power plants for five days amid what he described as "very good and productive" conversations. Tehran denied any negotiations had taken place, with Iranian state media claiming Trump "withdrew his 48-hour ultimatum out of fear of Iran's response".[2]

items.title: Zelensky warns Patriot missile deficit is inevitable as Iran war drains stockpiles

featured_image.name: Zelensky floats swapping Patriot missiles for interceptor drones amid ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has sounded the alarm that the expanding U.S.-Israeli war with Iran is siphoning critical military resources and diplomatic attention away from Ukraine, warning that Russian President Vladimir Putin stands to gain from a prolonged conflict in the Middle East.

"I have a very bad feeling about the impact of this war on the situation in Ukraine and the focus of America — it's more on the Middle East than on Ukraine, unfortunately," Zelensky told the BBC's Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg program in an interview that aired over the weekend. "Our diplomatic meetings, trilateral meetings, are constantly postponed. There is one reason: war in Iran."[1]

items.title: Trump claims Iran agreed to give up nuclear program as Tehran denies any talks

featured_image.name: Iran: Trump demands unconditional surrender in war - CNBC

items.description: President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that the United States and Iran have reached "major points of agreement" on a deal to end the nearly four-week-old war, claiming Tehran has agreed to abandon its nuclear weapons program and proposing joint US-Iran management of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign ministry flatly denied any negotiations are taking place.

items.title: Russia and Vietnam sign deal to build Vietnam's first nuclear plant

featured_image.name: Russia, Vietnam Sign Nuclear Energy Deal

items.description: Russia and Vietnam on Monday signed an intergovernmental agreement on the construction of Vietnam's first nuclear power plant, a milestone deal finalized during Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh's official visit to Moscow amid an escalating energy crisis driven by the war in the Middle East.

items.title: Europe's Stoxx 600 enters correction as Middle East crisis escalates

featured_image.name: European stocks slide, gas prices soar on Iran war

items.description: European stocks plunged into correction territory on Monday as the escalating conflict between Iran and the United States sent oil prices surging and rattled investors across global markets. The pan-European Stoxx 600 fell more than 2% to a four-month low, leaving it more than 11% below its February peak, according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: EU-Mercosur trade deal to take effect May 1

featured_image.name: EU and South America’s Mercosur bloc announce ‘win-win’ free trade deal

items.description:
The European Commission announced on Monday that its free trade agreement with the South American Mercosur bloc will provisionally enter into force on May 1, a landmark step that creates one of the world's largest free trade zones linking more than 700 million people and economies accounting for 25 percent of global GDP.[1][2]

The Commission said it had formally notified Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay of the provisional application date, calling it "an important step in demonstrating our credibility as a major trading partner". The deal will begin eliminating tariffs on more than 90 percent of trade between the two blocs.[2][1]
